research.interest: Logging a barbell program so the next session's load is decided by what I actually lifted
research.desired_outcome: Walk into the gym knowing exactly what goes on the bar and walk out with the evidence that sets next week
practice: Run a written block like 5x5 LP and add load session by session until a lift stalls
Log every working set between sets with chalk on both hands and the phone on the rack
Deload a stalled lift on purpose and pick the progression back up from a lighter load
Watch estimated one-rep max per main lift to see whether the block is still working
existing_artifacts: a notes app full of lines like squat 5x5 100kg
a printed program sheet in the gym bag
an export from an old tracker
constraints: capture must survive chalky hands and take under ten seconds
loads stay in the unit they were lifted in
effort words stay exactly as written
works offline in a basement gym
open_questions: whether accessory work needs the same detail as main lifts
whether bodyweight belongs in the same log
whether the bar weight varies between gyms
usage_context: phone propped on the rack between sets
laptop on Sunday when the next block gets written
research.first_value: File one set the way you would say it out loud and watch it land under today's prescribed day

evidence.claim: A serious training tracker keeps exercises as a canonical catalog with category and equipment rather than free text retyped into every session.
Plans days and sets are separated structures — a plan prescribes days, a day prescribes sets of an exercise, and a separate log records what was actually lifted.
evidence.locator: workout plan, day, set, and workout log structures

evidence.claim: Stable identities and relationships should be explicit and enforceable rather than repeated as text fields.
A filed set is an observation made by one agent at one time; a correction records the change without erasing what was first written.
A derived value is generated from observations and stays traceable to them rather than being stored as an independent fact.
Indexes should follow concrete filtering, joining, and ordering workloads.
Global and local example-driven alternatives support meaningful concept exploration and remix.
Begin with user needs and real context, then do the hard work required to make the service simple.
Keyboard access, focus, reflow, labels, status, and error recovery are release requirements.

concepts.title: Session Logbook
concepts.thesis: Capture the set while the plates are still on the bar and let the block assemble itself from filed work.
concepts.primary_loop: Open to today's day, file the set you just did, and put the phone back on the rack.
concepts.primary_affordance: A thumb-height set row prefilled with the prescribed scheme and load
concepts.differentiator: The only concept that files a real set between sets without a menu
feature_boundary: set capture with scheme and load
effort and RPE on the set that earned it
tradeoffs: trends arrive only after sets accumulate

concepts.title: Program Board
concepts.thesis: Make the written block the interface and treat the log as adherence against it.
concepts.primary_loop: Lay out the block by day, tick prescribed work as it lands, and let a stall trigger the deload.
concepts.primary_affordance: A week-by-day board of prescribed lifts with adherence marks
concepts.differentiator: Best answer to whether the block is being run as written
tradeoffs: one-off sessions outside the block feel foreign

concepts.title: Strength Curve
concepts.thesis: Treat every working set as a point on a strength curve and let the estimated one-rep max drive the next target.
concepts.primary_loop: Pick a main lift, read its e1RM line across the block, and set the next load from the curve.
concepts.primary_affordance: An e1RM line per main lift with the filed sets plotted beneath it
concepts.differentiator: Turns scattered numbers into whether the training is actually working
feature_boundary: e1RM estimation from load and reps
tradeoffs: needs months of filed sets before it pays off

fragments.fragment: prescribed-day strip above the set row
fragments.reason: Capture is fastest when today's prescription is already on screen to accept or overwrite.

fragments.fragment: e1RM trend rail beside the filed set
fragments.reason: One glance tells the lifter whether the block is still progressing without leaving capture.

user_decisions: Loads are in kg and the bar is 20 kg
Capture between sets has to take under ten seconds with one thumb
A grind is data — effort words stay verbatim on the set that earned them
A deload is a planned state of the block, not a missed week

relationships.description: Every session is trained inside one block.
Every filed set belongs to the session it was lifted in.
Every filed set names one catalog movement.
Prescribed work belongs to the block that wrote it.
Prescribed work points at the same catalog movement the log will use.

constraints.reason: The catalog holds one squat rather than five spellings of it.
A filed load stays inside what a barbell can physically hold.
RPE is a 1 to 10 effort scale and anything outside it is a typo.
A scheme like 5x5 always resolves to positive sets and reps.
An optional bodyweight is either plausible or rejected before storage.
A block cannot be completed before it has run and a deload is a state it passes through.

indexes.reason: Today's session is looked up by block and date on every capture.
The prescribed day is read in written order before the first set.
Every trend for one lift reads its sets in session order.
A PR is the heaviest load at one rep range for one lift.

workloads.question: What does today's day prescribe and what have I actually filed against it?
filters: block status is running or deloading
workloads.expected_scale: fewer than ten prescribed items per day
workloads.acceptance: Every prescribed lift shows its target beside what was filed, and unfiled work is obvious at arm's length.

workloads.question: Is my e1RM on this main lift still going up across the block?
workloads.expected_scale: hundreds of working sets per lift per year
workloads.acceptance: e1RM is computed from load and reps with Epley at read time and never stored, and every point links back to the set that produced it.

workloads.question: How many working sets did each movement category get this week?
workloads.expected_scale: tens of working sets per week
workloads.acceptance: Squat hinge press pull and carry volume add up per week with accessory work counted apart from main lifts.

workloads.question: What is my best load at each rep range for this lift?
workloads.expected_scale: thousands of filed sets across the catalog
workloads.acceptance: A PR is reported per lift per rep range and never as one unqualified number.

visual_world.name: Chalk and Platform
visual_world.mood: Chalked hands on a rubber platform — plain, unhurried, and legible at arm's length
visual_world.typography: A condensed grotesque for lift names with tabular monospaced numerals for load, reps, and RPE so columns line up between sets
visual_world.color_strategy: Platform black and chalk white with competition-plate colour carrying meaning — blue for the working load and red for a top set or a PR — and nothing else coloured
visual_world.layout_principle: The set row sits under the thumb at the bottom of the viewport; the prescribed day and the trend unfold behind it rather than as a dashboard grid
visual_world.density: Loose and thumb-sized between sets, tight and aligned when reading a whole block
signature_elements: loaded-barbell plate diagram that draws the actual plates per side for the top set
e1RM trend rail with the working-set band behind it
program-day checklist strip showing prescribed work against what was filed

views.title: The Platform
views.purpose: File the set you just did in under ten seconds and see it land under today's prescribed day.
views.layout: The set row dominates the lower half within thumb reach; the prescribed day strip sits above it and the plate diagram to its side.

actions.label: Start the session
actions.consequence: Opens today's session against the running block and loads the prescribed day.

actions.label: File this set
actions.consequence: Files the scheme and load against today's session and keeps the effort words verbatim on the set that earned them.

actions.label: Correct the set
actions.consequence: Keeps the original filed load and wording and records the correction beside it.

views.title: The Block
views.purpose: Run the written block, see adherence day by day, and call the deload on purpose.
views.layout: The day board leads at full reading width; the week's working-set split sits beside it as evidence rather than decoration.

actions.label: Start a block
actions.consequence: Writes the block's days and progression rule and moves it from planned to running.

actions.label: Call the deload
actions.consequence: Moves the running block into deloading and drops every prescribed load by the block's deload rule without rewriting past sessions.

views.title: Strength Curve
views.purpose: Read whether a main lift is still progressing and set the next target from the curve.
views.layout: The e1RM line fills the stage with filed sets plotted beneath it; the PR board aligns per rep range in a comparison rail.

actions.label: Show the sets behind this
actions.consequence: Opens the exact sets and sessions that produced the selected point on the curve.

views.title: The Rack
views.purpose: Keep one canonical movement per lift so every set files against the same thing.
views.layout: The movement catalog leads grouped by pattern; the selected lift's facts and bests sit in an inspector margin.

actions.label: Add a movement
actions.consequence: Puts one canonical lift in the catalog with its pattern, unit, and bar weight.

actions.label: Retire it
actions.consequence: Removes the lift from capture without touching the sets already filed against it.

release_thresholds.schema: all identity, relationship, constraint, and state-transition cases pass
release_thresholds.experience: the first-set and call-the-deload flows pass on phone and desktop
release_thresholds.evidence: every entity and critical view has an approved derivation

derivations.decision: Separate the movement, the block, the prescription, the session, and the set so the catalog, the plan, the event, and the observation each keep their own lifecycle.
Keep the lifter's shorthand verbatim in scheme and resolve it into sets and reps beside it, because 5x5 is how the work is said and five sets of five is how it must be queried.
derivations.user_decision: Capture between sets has to take under ten seconds with one thumb

derivations.decision: Hold the effort words on the set that earned them rather than flattening them into a session note.
derivations.user_decision: A grind is data — effort words stay verbatim on the set that earned them

derivations.decision: Model deloading as a real state of the block with transitions in and out, so a lighter week is intentional training rather than a hole in the data.
derivations.user_decision: A deload is a planned state of the block, not a missed week

derivations.decision: Compute e1RM from load and reps with the Epley estimate at read time and never store it, so the estimate stays traceable to the sets behind it and changes when a set is corrected.
Mark bodyweight sensitive and keep it out of exports by default because it is the one number a lifter does not want leaving the device.
Anchor the app on the set row rather than a summary dashboard because capture happens standing at the rack between sets.

derivations.decision: Use a platform-black chalk world with competition-plate colour carrying meaning instead of neon fitness gradients, so colour marks a top set rather than decorating the screen.
